entry.title: A hyperbolic area proof of the Kahn-Lyubich Covering Lemma and its generalization
entry.summary: The Covering Lemma of J. Kahn and M. Lyubich is a fundamental analytic tool for controlling conformal moduli of annuli under branched coverings of finite degree. In the last several decades, it has played a crucial role in establishing rigidity of multicritical polynomial and rational maps. The classical proof uses the Near-Degenerate Regime as the main mechanism. In this short note, we prove this lemma using hyperbolic area and the Dirichlet energy. We also establish a version of the Covering Lemma for holomorphic maps of infinite degree. Our argument is inspired by recent applications of the hyperbolic area method to the study of wandering domains in rational and transcendental dynamics.

entry.title: The Cauchy problem for skew-torsion-parallel spinors with applications to supergravity
entry.summary: We solve the Cauchy problem for an irreducible real spinor parallel with respect to a metric connection with skew-symmetric torsion on a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold, proving that it is well-posed modulo an obstruction that we identify explicitly, and obtaining an initial-data characterization of such spinors. Our proof relies on the theory of spinorial forms, which we use to explicitly integrate the coupled flow for the spinor and underlying metric via a rotated pull-back action of the flow generated by a vector field on the Cauchy hypersurface $Σ$. We characterize the corresponding constraint equations as an explicit exterior differential system and describe all its solutions in terms of contact structures and flat foliations, obtaining a complete classification in the compact case. In particular, we conclude that every oriented compact three-manifold arises as the Cauchy hypersurface of a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold equipped with a skew-torsion parallel spinor. Building on these results, we study the interaction between the four-dimensional Neveu-Schwarz supergravity evolution flow on an abelian bundle gerbe and the spinorial evolution flow determined by its supersymmetric conditions, which we prove to be well-posed and compatible. This establishes the well-posedness of the supersymmetric Neveu-Schwarz system in four dimensions and provides an initial-data characterization of supersymmetry. Furthermore, we obtain a strong rigidity result stating that every globally hyperbolic supersymmetric Neveu-Schwarz solution with a compact Cauchy hypersurface is flat and has vanishing bundle-gerbe curvature.

entry.title: $C^{1,α}$ Regularity of $W^{2,2}$ $Q$-Valued Maps with Small Laplacian
entry.summary: We establish a regularity criterion for $Q$-valued maps $u\in W^{2,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(Ω,\mathcal A_Q(\mathbb R^k))$, where $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$ is open. If $|Δu|\leqδ_*|D^2u|$ almost everywhere, with $δ_*=δ_*(n,k,Q)>0$ sufficiently small, then $u\in C^{1,α}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for some $α=α(n,k,Q)>0$, with quantitative estimates. The result holds for arbitrary $n\geq2$, $k\geq1$, and $Q\geq1$. The proof establishes uniform energy decay using a rigidity principle for positive-semidefinite matrix-valued measures with an aperture bound and approximately atomic divergence, extending the target-stress argument for the homogeneity gap in \cite{Luc26}. The argument relies only on first variation identities. As consequences, we obtain $C^{1,α}$ regularity for Dirichlet-stationary $W^{2,2}$ maps and for locally Lipschitz $W^{2,2}$ maps whose graph varifolds are stationary and have sufficiently small slope. Combining the latter result with Bellettini's Lipschitz sheeting theorem \cite{Bel25}, we establish $C^{1,α}$ sheeting in the multiple-valued sense for two-sided stable minimal immersions whose singular set has vanishing $2$-capacity relative to the immersion, under suitable flatness and mass bounds. Our results allow us to reduce the proof of compactness within this class, under locally uniform mass bounds, to the conjecture that branch sets of stationary $C^{1,α}$ multiple-valued graphs in codimension one have vanishing $2$-capacity.

entry.title: Countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit
entry.summary: We study countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit. Given an infinite compact metric countable space $X$, we show that $\mathcal{DO}(X)$, the collection of continuous functions on $X$ to itself admitting a dense orbit, is always nonempty. We then classify the systems in $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ up to topological conjugacy in terms of the second Cantor--Bendixson derivative $X^{(2)}$: if $X^{(2)} = \emptyset$ then all systems in $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ are mutually conjugate, while if $X^{(2)} \neq \emptyset$ then $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ contains $2^{\aleph_0}$ pairwise nonconjugate systems. The proof of the latter relies on a gluing construction for countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit, which is of independent interest. We also show that $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ is nowhere dense in $C(X,X)$ with the compact-open topology. We also study the Ellis semigroup $E(X,f)$ of a countable dynamical system. We characterize, under the assumption that $|ω(x,f)| = 1$ for each $x \in X^{(1)}$, when the nontrivial functions of $E(X,f)$ are continuous. In particular, for the family constructed on spaces with $|X^{(2)}| \geq 2$, every nontrivial function of the Ellis semigroup is discontinuous.

entry.title: Three-ends Furstenberg estimates and approximate rectangles
entry.summary: We prove a three-ends incidence estimate whose multiplicity exponent is sharp for one-dimensional Katz-Tao point sets.} At the heart of the argument lies rectangular non-concentration and its incidence theory introduced earlier by the authors. As an application, we obtain a strong quantitative bound on the number of approximate rectangles with the vertices belonging to four separated camps, each retaining a non-concentration condition.

entry.title: A counterexample to fixed-profile soliton resolution for the three-dimensional quintic wave equation
entry.summary: We consider the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation. We construct a bounded forward-global solution which starts arbitrarily close to a sign-changing stationary state and is asymptotic to a varying stationary profile plus one free wave. The core has two limits in distinct similarity orbits. A single energy-space norm identity identifies the radiation and reduces every competing fixed list to one profile; the two limits then give a contradiction. The construction uses summable radiation packets whose quadratic impulses produce fixed shape displacements on increasing time scales. We control the nonlinear error uniformly over these intervals and select the endpoints by a compact fixed-point map. A computer-assisted certificate validates the stationary state and its complete odd energy kernel.

entry.title: Well-Balanced WE-PINNs for the Shallow Water Equations over Smooth and Discontinuous Bathymetries
entry.summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) solve partial differential equations without a mesh, but they do not in general preserve the steady states that well-balanced schemes reproduce exactly. We present a well-balanced extension of the weak and entropy PINN (WE-PINN) framework to the shallow water equations over smooth and discontinuous bathymetry. The residual is a weak space--time control-volume identity enforced on randomly placed control volumes that may overlap, so no mesh is needed. In free-surface variables, the geometric source is integrated by parts onto the bed, so that the network is never differentiated, and a cell-local bed-slope correction makes the quadrature reproduce the exact bed increment. Bed discontinuities, located from the bathymetry alone, separate sub-domains carrying independent networks, coupled through conservation of discharge and total head. We prove that the fully discrete residual vanishes identically on the lake at rest for any control-volume family, quadrature order and nominal bed slope, so that the equilibrium is an exact global minimiser of the training objective; that the continuous residual characterises weak solutions; that the slope correction is consistent; and that no approximation with a continuous free surface can satisfy the head condition at a step with non-zero discharge, so that the decomposition is necessary. Numerically, the residual vanishes to round-off on four lake-at-rest configurations over smooth, discontinuous, compound and tabulated beds, and the trained network reaches the equilibrium to round-off under an extended training budget. On seven Riemann problems at a bottom step, covering sub-, super- and critical transitions, the network attains relative $L^1$ free-surface errors between $6.9\times10^{-4}$ and $3.5\times10^{-3}$, and reaches critical states without prescribing them.

entry.title: Fictitious Play When Agents Are Not Expected-Utility Maximizers: A Geometric Analysis in $2$-Action Games
entry.summary: Fictitious play (FP) is one of the earliest and most fundamental learning procedures in games, where each agent independently chooses a best response to the empirical distribution of opponents' past actions by maximizing the expected payoff with respect to it. However, learning agents may not always be expected-utility maximizers: they may use nonlinear evaluation functionals to account for the uncertainty induced by the opponents, e.g., via risk measures. In this work, we study nonlinear fictitious play (NL-FP), in which each pure action is evaluated by a general, possibly nonlinear functional of the payoff distribution induced by the opponent's empirical belief. To analyze NL-FP, we first identify a single-crossing property (SCP) of evaluation functionals that preserves the classical geometry of FP in $2\times2$ games. Furthermore, we conduct a novel geometric analysis of the convergence behavior of NL-FP in $2\times2$ games, even when the SCP fails. Beyond $2\times2$ games, we show that the convergence of NL-FP in $2\times n$ ($n\ge3$) games may fail even for continuous-time NL-FP, when the two-action player uses conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) in a $2\times3$ game. In addition, we identify a finite-crossing condition that ensures convergence of the selected continuous-time dynamics and the discrete-time iterates in general $2\times n$ games, which also provides new insights into the global landscape of continuous-time classical FP in such games.

entry.title: $C^*$-selflessness for free Burnside groups
entry.summary: The free Burnside group $B(m,n)$ is obtained from the free group of rank $m$ by imposing the relations $w^n=1$ for all words $w$. We prove that $B(m,n)$ is completely $C^*$-selfless for every $m\geq2$ and every odd exponent $n\geq557$. Consequently, its reduced group $C^*$-algebra has stable rank one and strict comparison of positive elements by its canonical trace. This answers the question of whether $C^*$-selfless groups can satisfy a nontrivial group law. The proof establishes Ozawa's property $P_{PHP}$ by combining a combinatorial construction with a relative power-avoidance argument based on the canonical forms of Atkarskaya-Rips-Tent.

entry.title: Toward the abelian category of positive Lagrangians
entry.summary: We introduce a geometric construction whose terminal configuration determines the kernel and cokernel of a morphism between positive Lagrangian branes in the derived Fukaya category of a Calabi-Yau manifold. Thus, if the construction always terminates, the full subcategory of positive Lagrangian branes is abelian, as conjectured by Joyce. We show that this abelian category admits Harder-Narasimhan filtrations with respect to the central charge defined by the holomorphic volume form. Under appropriate split-generation assumptions, we construct a Bridgeland stability condition whose stable objects are isomorphic to special Lagrangian branes, as predicted by the Thomas-Yau conjecture. The geometric construction is based on a one-parameter family of special Lagrangian submanifolds with boundary. One part of the boundary is contained in the Lagrangian underlying the domain of the morphism and the other in the Lagrangian underlying the codomain. Surgeries occur as the family encounters singularities or obstruction walls. We prove that the construction always terminates for the two-torus and provide higher dimensional examples.
